newsitem.title: UK: Willis year profits show strong rise.
newsitem.headline: Willis year profits show strong rise.

text.p: Willis Corroon Group Plc, the international insurance broker, announced a rise in 1996 profits on Thursday but warned that insurance rates continue to fall and sustained strength in sterling could affect 1997 figures.

Pre-tax profits for the 12 months to December 31 rose to 91.6 million pounds ($149.7 million), an increase of 83 percent over the same period last year, which included 30 million pounds in exceptionals.
Before exceptionals and disposals, profits from continuing operations were 13 percent higher than the last year at 89.1 million pounds. Dividend was maintained at 6.6 pence.

Willis said that insurance rates continue to decline almost universally, with particiularly sharp reductions in sectors served by its London-based global speciality businesses, and competition in the U.S. retail market was intensifying.
The recent rise in sterling, if sustained, would also hit 1997 results, it said, and profits from its Lloyd's members agency were unlikely to be repeated at the 1996 level.
However, the group said it expects to benefit from the clear strategies and targets now established for each business unit and a change programme designed to enhance performance and competitiveness.

Willis executive chairman John Reeve said the increase in profits, a rise in shareholders funds of 31.3 million pounds and elimination of net debt were evidence of the successful implementation of plans to restore the group's financial health.
"The Group is now focused on its core operation, following a programme of disposal, profitability has been improved and the balance sheet has been significantly strengthened," said Reeve.
During 1996 the group concentrated on the development of a strategy supported by specific operational plans and targets.
These were designed to identify and exploit growth opportunities, enhance service and operational capabilities and improve client focus, said Reeve.
Following the implementation of the Lloyd's Reconstruction and Renewal plan (R&R) the group's members agency earned profit commission for the first time since 1992.

The 14.5 million pound profit for the 1993 year included reserves for prior years released by Equitas, the Lloyd's vehicle set up to take on the losses run up by the insurance market between 1988 and 1992.
This was partly offset by contributions of 6.3 million pounds to the R&R plan.
Willis said present indications were that the agency's profit commission on the 1994 year of account, receivable in 1997, will be around half those of the 1993 year.

Sterling's recent rise had an adverse impact on 1996 profits to the extent of 3.1 million pounds and the results included severance costs of 11.3 million pounds. These arose primarily from the implementation of the group's change programme and are expected to produce cost savings in 1997 and beyond.
By year end total staff numbers in continuing operations had fallen 11 percent to 9,116.

Brokerage and fee revenue in continuing operations grew three percent to 683.2 million pounds, but premium rates continue to suffer from frequently severe falls. Retail operations also faced continuing rate declines. ($1=.6120 Pound)
